nps_overview.regulator: PFRDA (Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority)

section_80ccd_1.limit: 10% of salary (included in 80C limit of ₹1.5 lakh)

section_80ccd_2.limit: 14% of salary for central govt, 10% for others

tier_1.lock_in: Exit eligibility depends on age, vesting period, subscriber model and current PFRDA rules; some eligible non-government normal exits may occur after a qualifying 15-year vesting period.
tier_1.maturity: For eligible non-government normal exits effective 16 Dec 2025: up to 80% lump sum and at least 20% annuity, subject to corpus thresholds; tax treatment is separate.

fund_managers: Aditya Birla Sun Life Pension Management

faqs.question: What is the minimum contribution for NPS Tier I?
faqs.answer: PFRDA lists ₹500 minimum per Tier I contribution and ₹1,000 minimum per year for the All Citizen Model. Check current rules for your NPS model.

faqs.question: Can I withdraw money from NPS before 60?
faqs.answer: Partial withdrawal of up to 25% is allowed after 3 years for specific purposes like education, medical treatment, or home purchase.

faqs.question: What happens to NPS at age 60?
faqs.answer: Eligible non-government normal exits can allow up to 80% lump sum and at least 20% annuity, subject to corpus thresholds and current rules. Tax treatment is separate.

faqs.question: How much tax can I save with NPS?
faqs.answer: Tax deductions depend on tax regime. Under the old regime, 80CCD(1) and 80CCD(1B) may qualify subject to limits; under the new regime, personal contributions are not deductible, while eligible employer contribution under 80CCD(2) may qualify.

faqs.question: What is the expected return from NPS?
faqs.answer: Historical returns have been 8-12% annually depending on asset allocation. Equity-heavy allocations tend to give higher returns over long periods.
